questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good school and great weather. :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I could be a little difficult. It is nice to have someone who is also going to figure everything out with.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, you had to figure it out by yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Private, shared rooms or dorms. All of them are pretty expensive and not nice at all. I would recommend you to get something off campus. (In West Campus)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could get a meal plan, but i did not have it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Find something in West Campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Exchange students from UCPH are last in line to pick courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They did not offer the courses i hoped for and were offered every other year. But it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try figure it out in good time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was easier than back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is pretty different from Copenhagen. Your grades are based on participation, test, midterms and exams throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Methods of Environmental Policy Analysis
Foundations of Finance 
Industrial Organization
Economics of Auctions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Economics of Auctions very much. It was the best course i had and Professor Jorge Balat was very good. But if they had offered Game Theory i would choose that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The mandatory Health insurance though the school. It was around 11.000 DKK in total and only covered 80%. I also bought a danish insurance which covered 100% and also covered theft or if my computer or other electronics broke down. My normal insurance in Denmark only covered the first 60 days.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Healt Insurance and housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really nice facilities at the university.  The pool is so nice, we spend a lot time there the first months, but you can also use the gym or play a great amount of sports, like soccer, basketball, tennis, squash etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We made a soccer team with most of the Danes and signed up for the school tournament. Then you play a match every week. You can also just show up at field and play "Pick-up Ball". (Remember to pack your boots)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We drove to New Orleans a weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are friendly and especially when you are an exchange student.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It can get really cold, but in the summer it is like 40 degree celcius. Remember to pack a jacket and a sweater. The weather changes a lot in November/December. One day it is 25 degrees and the next it's 3. 

Use the facilities, they are great. 

Live off campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Have a good time and experience a totally different way of going to school.

questions.answer: Yes
